definitions.explanation: Colloquial form of いろいろな. Used to describe many different kinds.

examples.japanese: {色|いろ}んな{経験|けいけん}をした。
{色|いろ}んな{国|くに}に{行|い}った。
この{店|みせ}には{色|いろ}んな{種類|しゅるい}のパンがある。
examples.english: This shop has various kinds of bread.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}は{色|いろ}んなことに{興味|きょうみ}があった。
examples.english: When I was a child, I was interested in all sorts of things.

notes:
{色|いろ}んな is a colloquial contraction of いろいろな (various). Extremely common in spoken Japanese.

FORMALITY LEVELS:
- いろいろな: standard/formal (writing, polite speech)
- {色|いろ}んな: casual/colloquial (conversation, informal writing)
- いろんな: same word without kanji (also common)

GRAMMAR:
{色|いろ}んな is a pre-noun modifier only. It always precedes a noun and cannot be used as a predicate. Use いろいろだ for the predicative form.
- {色|いろ}んな{人|ひと}: various people ✓
- {人|ひと}は{色|いろ}んなだ: ✗ (use いろいろだ instead)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {色|いろ}んな{人|ひと}: various people
- {色|いろ}んな{場所|ばしょ}: various places
- {色|いろ}んな{意味|いみ}で: in various senses
- {色|いろ}んなことがある: all sorts of things happen
